info.title: OpenAsy Consent API
info.summary: Who agreed to what, on which channel and to which text, with İYS kept in step.
info.description:
Every screen of Consent uses this API, and so can your scripts and the other products (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only; anything removed is deprecated first (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

Purposes, their texts and the sites are set in the product's file, never through the API. The site's script at `/c/<site>.js` reads and sends `/api/v1/choices`. Everything else takes the session of a signed-in person or an API token, and each operation names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`: viewer, editor, admin; ADR 0003).

Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

get.description: Whether a person may be reached on a channel for a purpose: only while their latest answer for it is yes, to a version of the text the file still counts. Name the person by one of email, phone, id, browser or person. Messages, Analytics, Forms and Audience ask this before they act. Needs the viewer role.

parameters.description: The purpose's id in the file.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: The person's phone number, such as +905551112233.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Your own id for the person.

parameters.name: person
parameters.description: A person id this API returned.

200.description: The answer.

post.description: The same for up to 1000 people at once, such as a campaign's list, answered in the same order. Needs the viewer role.

Answers on the purpose kept in step with İYS are queued for İYS. Nothing recorded can be changed afterwards: a change of mind is a new answer. Needs the editor role.

post.description: A signed link to a site's preference page that shows this person's message purposes, for the footer of an email or an SMS. Needs the editor role.

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when Consent runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from the Consent origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings, API tokens (`oa_consent_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

adminToken.description: Only when Consent is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

ConfigFile.description: The file and whether it is applied; null before it was first read.

connected.description: The file sets iys and both its environment variables are set.

iys.description: Answers on its email, SMS and call channels are kept in step with İYS.

current.description: The version people are asked now.

from.description: When it came into force: from in the file, or the day it was first applied.

granted.description: People whose latest answer is yes to this version.

renew.description: Yes to a version the file has since asked again for.

Who.description: One or more ways the person is known. Emails are lowercased, phone numbers written as +905551112233.

status.description: granted: the latest answer is yes; withdrawn: no; renew: yes, to a text the file has since asked again for; none: never answered.

allowed.description: Whether the person may be reached on this channel for this purpose now.

person.description: Null when nobody is known by these identifiers, or they name two people.

version.description: The version of the text the person saw; by default the one in force at `at`.

at.description: When they answered; now by default. Never in the future.

iysSource.description: Where İYS is told it was given, such as HS_CAGRI_MERKEZI; the file's iys.source by default.

proof.description: What shows the answer was given: a form's name, a call's reference.

via.description: Where the answers came from, such as forms/newsletter.

actor.description: Who recorded it: a member's email or token:<name>.

latest.description: The latest answer on each purpose and channel the person answered.

conflict.description: İYS and the record disagree on at least one channel.

counts.description: The later of the two, which decides.

reach.description: People who may be reached now, by purpose and channel.

iysRefusals.description: Refusals sent to İYS for the channels the person had said yes to.

token.description: A preference link's token; needed for message purposes.
